title: Probe-driven kernel dispatch with circuit-breaker for speculative decoding routing
creator: Miguel Santos
description:
Background:
We need a lightweight, probe-driven dispatch layer that selects compute kernels and model variants for speculative decode paths while protecting stable decoding via a circuit-breaker when probes indicate instability. Current heuristic routing adds tails under load and has limited kernel-awareness. This ticket designs and implements a probe-based dispatcher + soft circuit-breaker that: (1) runs micro-prefill probes to measure acceptance confidence and kernel latency signatures, (2) uses a compact decision function to route speculative vs stable decodes and to select kernel variants, and (3) trips a soft circuit-breaker to fallback to safe decode paths when acceptance or latency budgets are violated.

Goals:
- Reduce end-to-end P95 generation latency for common interactive workloads by 8-12% while keeping error/regression rate <= 0.5% relative to baseline model output quality checks.
- Ensure per-request latency budgets are respected: probes must add <= 2ms median overhead and <= 8ms 95th overhead for requests flagged as speculative-eligible.
- Provide clear telemetry: acceptance_rate, probe_latency_signature, kernel_mismatch_count, circuit_breaker_state, and fallback_reason.

Scope:
In scope: probe design, kernel dispatch policy, soft circuit-breaker implementation, rollout toggles, metrics, unit/integration tests, and a canary rollout with telemetry dashboards.
Out of scope: model architecture changes, quantization engine changes, and non-speculative routing paths (those remain unchanged).

Design summary:
- Probe behaviour: run a short prefill probe (8-16 tokens, beam=1, low-temp) on a lightweight kernel-path (fast quantized kernel) to compute two signals: acceptance_score (log-prob delta vs baseline prefix) and kernel_latency_signature (per-layer average ms). Probe runs in the same request allocation but on a reserved micro-batch to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Decision function: a compact linear scoring function combining acceptance_score, recent probe_success_rate (EWMA over 1 minute), and kernel_latency_signature delta. Tunable thresholds: ACCEPT_T (defaults: 0.85 acceptance_score, 1.25 latency_ratio), SOFT_TRIP_T (failures over 5% of last 100 probes trips soft breaker), HARD_TRIP_T (>=15% failures in last 100 trips causes hard fallback to safe decode).
- Kernel dispatch: prefer fast-kernel variants (int4/int8 fused kernels) for speculative decode when acceptance and latency ratios permit; otherwise prefer stable-kernel path. KernelFingerprints maintained per-model+sequence-length bucket updated by background prober.
- Circuit-breaker: three states (Closed, Soft-Open, Open). Soft-Open reduces speculative routing rate by multiplicative factor and forces conservative kernels; Open disables speculative routing for the model+tenant for an exponentially increasing cooldown. State persists in runtime metadata with TTL and is surfaced in logs and tracing spans.

Trade-offs considered:
- Probe cost vs value: probes add overhead; we target micro-probes with strict time budget and fall back to default paths when probe resources are scarce.
- Complexity vs maintainability: decision function remains linear with <8 features to keep runtime hot-path simple and auditable.
- Data staleness: use short EWMA windows (1m) for agile reaction but persist longer-term statistics to aid offline tuning.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag gated by model+tenant. Start with internal canary on 10% of requests for two non-critical tenants.
2) Observe telemetry for 72 hours. Key thresholds: probe_overhead_95 < 8ms, acceptance_drop < 0.5%, P95_gen_latency improvement >= 5% on canary.
3) Expand to 50% if safe, then gradual ramp to 100% for eligible tenants.
4) If Soft-Open triggers frequently, auto-reduce speculative percentage and alert oncall.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- New metrics: speculative_probe_latency_ms_{p50,p95}, acceptance_rate_{model,tenant}, kernel_latency_ratio, cb_state_count, fallback_rate, quality_regressions_detected.
- Dashboards: runtime->spec-decode->canary-overview and alerts for: fallback_rate > 1% sustained, acceptance_rate drop > 0.5% absolute, probe_overhead_95 > 10ms.

Testing:
- Unit: decision function boundary tests, circuit-breaker state transitions, kernel selection logic.
- Integration: simulate mixed traffic using load harness (tools/bench/spec-decode-sim) with recorded real traffic traces.
- E2E: Canary on internal tenant with golden evaluation prompts and automated diffs for regressions.

Deliverables:
- Runtime dispatcher implementation (C++/Rust module) and control-plane flags (k8s config + feature toggle).
- Telemetry + dashboards (Grafana + observability hooks).
- Docs: PRD section, runtime README, rollout checklist.

Success criteria:
- Passes canary without quality/regression flags for 72 hours and achieves targeted latency improvements.
- Telemetry shows circuit-breaker behaving as expected during injected failures.

Open questions:
- Should probes be token-preserving for KV cache warmup? (trade-off: longer probe warms cache but costs more latency).
- How to prioritize kernel selection across multi-tenant GPU sharing? (we propose tenant-scoped kernel fingerprints first).
